answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by binding identity to unique-work puzzles tied to hardware attestation: before transacting, an agent solves a cryptographic puzzle derived from its machine identity, so fake accounts cost real silicon instead of free email addresses. When every bid carries a nonce minted by a trusted enclave, clones drifting across the lagoon of low-reputation accounts cannot amortize that cost, while a genuine worker keeps one ember of reputation alive over months. On the horizon of cooperation grows a trail of solved work sybils cannot fabricate.
